title: Britain's New Guide: Be Ready for 72 Hours on Your Own
summary: Imagine your phone, lights and fridge all stopped working. What would your family do for three days? Britain is now asking everyone that question, with a new national guide called 'Be Ready.' The guide explains how to look after yourself for 72 hours in an emergency, such as a big storm or a cyberattack that knocks out computers. It suggests keeping extra food, water, medicines and a torch at home. The last national campaign was in 1980, during the Cold War, when the government sent out leaflets called 'Protect and Survive.' People laughed at it. This time, officials say they want calm, useful tips, not scary messages. The head of the British Army, General Sir Roland Walker, told soldiers the world is in 'extreme jeopardy' and leaders need to talk honestly about risks. Disaster expert Lucy Easthope says the public wants reassurance. 'This is reawakening the idea that it's perfectly survivable,' she said. Other countries in Europe have also updated their advice. The guide's message is simple: a little planning now can make a hard few days much easier.
why_it_matters: If the lights went out at your house, knowing what your family has ready at home would help you feel safe instead of scared.
